Answer: B
Reason: Although the automated report describes normal contours, visual inspection of Figure 1 reveals a prominent right descending pulmonary artery (pruned appearance) and enlarged central pulmonary arteries, which are classic radiographic signs of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension; option B correctly identifies this specific morphological finding and its association with mild pulmonary hypertension, whereas other options describe normal vessels or incorrect laterality. *(guided by t000002)*
